results.title: New Zealand unveils new sanctions against Russia
results.description: Wellington, Aug 8 (IANS) New Zealand on Saturday announced a new round of sanctions against those supporting Russia's conflict with Ukraine. Thirty-three individuals and entities were targeted in the sanctions package unveiled by Foreign Minister Winston Peters. New Zealand enforced the Russia Sanctions Act in March 2022 and has moved against more than 2,000 individuals, entities and vessels ever since in its 36 rounds of sanctions, reports Xinhua news agency. In a separate development, the US Senate passed a sweeping Russia sanctions bill that does not name India but could expose it and other major buyers of Russian energy to tariffs of up to 100 per cent. Passed by the Senate by an 86-11 vote, the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 now goes to the House of Representatives, where senior Democrats have objected to its tariff provisions. The legislation requires the administration to identify countries using trade data rather than naming them in the statute. It covers the five largest importers of Russian crude oil, the five largest importers of Russian natural gas and the five leading countries facilitating Russian oil sanctions evasion. Those determinations would be based on the most recent 12-month period and reviewed every 180 days. The bill would impose primary and secondary sanctions against Russian officials, oligarchs, their family members, banks and financial institutions. It also targets foreign actors supporting Moscow's war in Ukraine and Russia's so-called shadow fleet used to transport oil and evade sanctions. The legislation was named after Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who negotiated an agreement with the White House before his sudden death on July 11. Senators accelerated work on the measure after his death. It would also extend the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 until 2031. The law penalises companies investing in Iran's energy sector. --IANS sd/

results.title: 7 killed, 11 injured in Himachal accident as bus rolls into 100-feet deep gorge in Chamba
results.description: Shimla, Aug 8 (IANS) At least seven people were killed and 11 were injured on Saturday when a private public transport bus rolled into a 100-feet deep gorge on the Tissa-Bairagarh route in Chamba district in Himachal Pradesh, police said. Most of the victims were locals and going to Chamba town. The dead included the driver and the conductor. The injured have been admitted to a hospital in Tissa town. According to preliminary information, there were approximately 20 to 25 passengers on board the bus at the time of the mishap. Chamba Superintendent of Police, Vijay Saklani, said the cause of the accident is yet be ascertained and the police would investigate the circumstances. Chaos ensued at the site after the accident. People in the area began rescue operations even before local authorities reached the spot. However, rescue operations gained momentum with the arrival of police and administrative teams. According to information, the bus owned by Sharma Travelers departed from Bairagarh for Chamba at around 6.30 a.m. The bus had only travelled three kms when near the Chaluj turn the driver lost control and the bus skidded off the road and fell into the gorge. The bus landed on the road beneath the accident spot. Eyewitnesses told the police that as the driver was negotiating a turn, the driver lost control of the vehicle and the bus rolled down the hill. Eyewitnesses said the administration had a tough time extricating the victims from the badly-mangled bus. Chamba is one of the remotest places in the state and scarcity and low frequency of passenger buses in the district often leads to overcrowding of the vehicles. Often the police blamed buses belonging to private operators and their “reckless, untrained drivers” for most of the fatal accidents in the state. The spot where the mishap took place has earned the notoriety of being accident-prone as it has seen several road accidents in the recent past. --IANS vg/rad
